revealWordProblem.title: Apply: School District Size
revealWordProblem.text: A large school district has 621,000 students in grades kindergarten through 12. The district currently has 1 teacher for every 20 students but plans to hire more teachers to have 1 teacher for every 15 students. How many teachers does the school district need to hire to reach its goal?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: The district hires 10,350 teachers. It currently has 621,000 ÷ 20 = 31,050 teachers, and it needs 621,000 ÷ 15 = 41,400 teachers to reach the new ratio. The difference is 41,400 − 31,050 = 10,350 teachers to hire.

visual.title: 1,344 ÷ 12, one place at a time
visual.caption: Long division writes one quotient digit per place: 1, 1, 2 — so each of the 12 sections gets 112 bars

conceptIntro.heading: Push further — How do you divide big numbers?
conceptIntro.intro: You already can do this. In this group we go deeper: trickier numbers, a second way to see it, and explaining why it works — not just getting the answer.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Repeat the cycle Divide → Multiply → Subtract → Bring Down until no digits are left to bring down; what is left at the end is the remainder — and you can explain why it works, even when it gets tricky.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: I want 1,344 ÷ 12. The dividend is 1,344 and the divisor is 12, so 12 goes outside the bracket and 1,344 goes inside.
DIVIDE: 12 does not fit into 1, so I look at 13. How many 12s fit into 13? One. I write 1 above the 3.
SUBTRACT: 13 − 12 = 1. That is what is left so far.
BRING DOWN: I bring the next digit, 4, down next to the 1 to make 14. Now I repeat the cycle.
REPEAT: 14 ÷ 12 → 1 (written above the 4), 1 × 12 = 12, 14 − 12 = 2, and I bring down the last 4 to make 24.
REPEAT: 24 ÷ 12 → 2 (written above the last 4), 2 × 12 = 24, 24 − 24 = 0. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 0.
The digits I wrote are 1, 1, 2, so 1,344 ÷ 12 = 112. I check by multiplying: 12 × 112 = 1,344.

explore.instructions: Go deeper: Divide 1,344 ÷ 12 with long division. Sort each card — is it a step in the divide, multiply, subtract, bring down cycle for this problem, or is it NOT a step in this division? As you work, ask yourself WHY it works.

items.text: DIVIDE: 12 fits into 13 one time, so write 1 above the 3.
BRING DOWN: bring the next 4 down to make 14.
REPEAT: 24 ÷ 12 → 2, then 24 − 24 = 0, so the remainder is 0.
Add the dividend and the divisor: 1,344 + 12 = 1,356.
Bring down two digits at once to make 134.
Write the leftover 1 into the quotient instead of above the bar.

onLevel.stem: A warehouse has 2,184 items to pack into boxes of 14. How many boxes are needed?

14 × 166 = 2,324, which is more items than the warehouse actually has. Check the tens digit of your quotient.
14 × 155 = 2,170, which leaves 14 items with no box. Multiply back to test whether your quotient uses up every item.
hints: The question asks how many groups of 14 fit into 2,184 — that phrase 'how many boxes' signals division.
Estimate to anchor yourself: 14 × 150 = 2,100 is close to 2,184. Then set it up as long division and run the cycle.
DIVIDE: 21 ÷ 14 → 1. MULTIPLY: 1 × 14 = 14. SUBTRACT: 21 − 14 = 7. BRING DOWN the 8 to make 78, then repeat the cycle.

onLevel.title: Spot the Mistake in 2,058 ÷ 14

workedExample.label: Problem
workedExample.work: Divide 2,058 ÷ 14 with long division. Dividend = 2,058, divisor = 14.

workedExample.label: Divide, Multiply, Subtract
workedExample.work: 14 does not fit into 2, so start with 20. 20 ÷ 14 → 1. 1 × 14 = 14, and 20 − 14 = 6

workedExample.label: Bring down, repeat
workedExample.work: Bring down the 5 to make 65. 65 ÷ 14 → 4. 4 × 14 = 56, and 65 − 56 = 9

workedExample.label: Bring down, repeat
workedExample.work: Bring down the 8 to make 98. 98 ÷ 14 → 8. 8 × 14 = 112, and 98 − 112 = −14

onLevel.correctWork: The DIVIDE step in the last cycle chose a digit that is too big: 8 × 14 = 112 is more than the 98 you have to subtract from, and you can never subtract more than the working number. The right digit is 7, since 7 × 14 = 98 and 98 − 98 = 0. The quotient is 147 with remainder 0, and 14 × 147 = 2,058 rebuilds the dividend.
hints: Look at the last cycle. After you MULTIPLY, the product has to be small enough to SUBTRACT from 98. Is 112?
A negative difference means the DIVIDE step picked too large a digit. Try the largest digit whose product with 14 still fits inside 98, then finish the cycle.
onLevel.explanation: The last DIVIDE step is where it breaks: the student wrote 8, but 8 × 14 = 112 is larger than the 98 they had to subtract from, so the difference came out negative. The largest digit that fits is 7, since 7 × 14 = 98 leaves 0, so the quotient is 147 and 14 × 147 = 2,058 checks out.
onLevel.explanationEs: El último paso DIVIDE es donde falla: el estudiante escribió 8, pero 8 × 14 = 112 es mayor que los 98 de los que tenía que restar, así que la diferencia salió negativa. El dígito más grande que cabe es 7, ya que 7 × 14 = 98 deja 0, así que el cociente es 147 y 14 × 147 = 2,058 lo comprueba.

onLevel.title: Find Sonia's Mistake

workedExample.label: Divide
workedExample.work: 16 does not fit into 1 or 15, so start with 153. 153 ÷ 16 → 9, written above the 3

onLevel.correctWork: The SUBTRACT step is wrong: 153 − 144 = 9, not 19. Long division has a built-in warning here — the difference after you subtract must always be SMALLER than the divisor, and 19 is bigger than 16. With the correct difference of 9, bring down the 6 to make 96, then DIVIDE 96 ÷ 16 → 6 and SUBTRACT 96 − 96 = 0. The quotient is 96 with remainder 0, and 16 × 96 = 1,536.
hints: After you SUBTRACT, compare the difference to the divisor. What should always be true about a difference of 19 when the divisor is 16?
Redo the subtraction 153 − 144 carefully, bring down the 6, and finish the cycle. Then test the result with 16 × quotient.
onLevel.explanation: Step 3 is the break: 153 − 144 = 9, not 19. Long division has a built-in warning here — if the difference after SUBTRACT is as big as the divisor, another whole group still fits. With the correct difference of 9, bringing down the 6 gives 96, and 96 ÷ 16 → 6 with nothing left, so the quotient is 96 and 16 × 96 = 1,536 confirms it.
onLevel.explanationEs: El Paso 3 es donde falla: 153 − 144 = 9, no 19. La división larga trae aquí un aviso incorporado: si la diferencia después de RESTAR es tan grande como el divisor, todavía cabe otro grupo entero. Con la diferencia correcta de 9, al bajar el 6 se forma 96, y 96 ÷ 16 → 6 sin que sobre nada, así que el cociente es 96 y 16 × 96 = 1,536 lo confirma.

onLevel.prompt: The station must load 3,360 ration packs equally into 14 storage pods. Solve it with long division. Name each step — divide, multiply, subtract, bring down — and check your answer by multiplying.
onLevel.sentenceFrame: 3,360 ÷ 14 = ___. I divided ___ by 14 and wrote ___ , then multiplied, subtracted and brought down the next digit each time. I checked by multiplying: 14 × ___ = 3,360.
hints: Re-read the sentence frame: it wants the four named steps — divide, multiply, subtract, bring down — not just the answer.
Set it up as 14 ⟌ 3,360. Since 14 does not fit into 3, your first working number is 33.
DIVIDE: 33 ÷ 14 → 2. MULTIPLY: 2 × 14 = 28. SUBTRACT: 33 − 28 = 5. BRING DOWN the 6 to make 56, then repeat — and watch what you must write when you bring down the final 0.
onLevel.explanation: Long division on 14 ⟌ 3,360 runs the cycle three times: 33 ÷ 14 → 2 (2 × 14 = 28, leaving 5), bring down the 6 → 56 ÷ 14 → 4 (4 × 14 = 56, leaving 0), bring down the 0 → 0 ÷ 14 → 0, so a 0 must be written in the ones place. The quotient is 240 ration packs per pod, and 14 × 240 = 3,360 proves none were left over.
onLevel.explanationEs: La división larga de 3,360 entre 14 repite el ciclo tres veces: 33 ÷ 14 → 2 (2 × 14 = 28, quedan 5), baja el 6 → 56 ÷ 14 → 4 (4 × 14 = 56, queda 0), baja el 0 → 0 ÷ 14 → 0, así que hay que escribir un 0 en las unidades. El cociente es 240 paquetes de raciones por cápsula, y 14 × 240 = 3,360 comprueba que no sobró ninguno.
onLevel.promptEs: La estación debe cargar 3,360 paquetes de raciones por partes iguales en 14 cápsulas de almacenamiento. Resuélvelo con división larga. Nombra cada paso — divide, multiplica, resta, baja — y comprueba tu respuesta multiplicando.
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer el modelo de oración: pide los cuatro pasos con su nombre — divide, multiplica, resta, baja — no solo la respuesta.
Escríbelo como 14 ⟌ 3,360. Como 14 no cabe en 3, tu primer número de trabajo es 33.
DIVIDE: 33 ÷ 14 → 2. MULTIPLICA: 2 × 14 = 28. RESTA: 33 − 28 = 5. BAJA el 6 para formar 56 y repite; fíjate en lo que debes escribir al bajar el último 0.

hintsEs: La división pregunta cuántos grupos de 12 caben dentro de 4,896, así que la respuesta debe estar en las centenas, no en las decenas.

25 × 389 = 9,725, which overshoots 7,225. Recheck the tens digit after you take out the first 200 groups of 25.

Set it up as long division and start the cycle: how many 25s fit into 72?

extending.stem: A school orders 3,648 pencils packed 24 to a box. How many boxes are there?

choiceFeedback: Re-read the problem carefully and try again.

workedExample.label: Problem
workedExample.work: Repair the machine for 3,724 ÷ 7. Dividend = 3,724, divisor = 7.

workedExample.label: Divide, Multiply, Subtract
workedExample.work: 7 does not fit into 3, so start with 37. 37 ÷ 7 → 5. 5 × 7 = 35, and 37 − 35 = 2

workedExample.label: Bring down, repeat
workedExample.work: Bring down the 2 to make 22. 22 ÷ 7 → 3. 3 × 7 = 21, and 22 − 21 = 1

workedExample.label: Final answer
workedExample.work: Nothing left to bring down. Quotient = 53, remainder = 1

extending.correctWork: The machine quit before the last digit. Look at 3,724 — the final 4 was never brought down. Bring it down next to the 1 to make 14, then run the cycle once more: DIVIDE 14 ÷ 7 → 2, MULTIPLY 2 × 7 = 14, SUBTRACT 14 − 14 = 0. The quotient is 532 with remainder 0, and the check 7 × 532 = 3,724 rebuilds the dividend.
hints: Look at the dividend 3,724. Which of its digits has the machine already used, and which one is still waiting to be brought down?
One digit is still waiting. Bring it down next to the leftover 1, run one more divide–multiply–subtract cycle, then test the result with 7 × quotient.
extending.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2 — Repara la máquina de arcade
extending.explanation: The machine stopped before the last digit: after subtracting 21 there was still a 4 in 3,724 waiting to be brought down. Bringing it down makes 14, and 14 ÷ 7 → 2 with 14 − 14 = 0, so the quotient is 532 with remainder 0. The check 7 × 532 = 3,724 rebuilds the dividend instead of the 372 the broken machine reported.
extending.explanationEs: La máquina se detuvo antes del último dígito: después de restar 21 todavía quedaba un 4 en 3,724 esperando bajar. Al bajarlo se forma 14, y 14 ÷ 7 → 2 con 14 − 14 = 0, así que el cociente es 532 con residuo 0. La comprobación 7 × 532 = 3,724 reconstruye el dividendo en vez del 372 que reportó la máquina dañada.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Divide Multi-Digit Numbers is skipping a placeholder zero in the quotient when a digit doesn't divide evenly, which shifts every digit after it out of place. For example, dividing 3,216 ÷ 3: 3 ÷ 3 = 1, but the next digit 2 doesn't divide by 3, so a 0 must be written before continuing — bring down the 1 to make 21 ÷ 3 = 7, then bring down 6 ÷ 3 = 2, giving the correct quotient 1,072. A student who skips writing that 0 and jumps straight to 21 ÷ 3 = 7 ends up with 172 instead of 1,072 — an answer off by a factor of ten. Always check: does a digit in your quotient go missing every time you 'can't divide'? If so, you dropped a placeholder zero.

connect.scenario: A school is ordering 1,680 pencils to distribute equally to 24 classrooms for the school year.
connect.promptQuestion: How does multi-digit division help the school figure out how many pencils each classroom gets?

check.stem: Estimate first: rounding to 1,600 ÷ 20 gives about how many pencils per room?
check.explanation: 1,600 ÷ 20 = 80, so the exact answer should land near 80. Getting 70 is reasonable; getting 7 or 700 would signal a place-value slip.

check.stem: If the pencils were split among 20 classrooms instead of 24, would each room get more or fewer?
choices: More, because the pencils are split among fewer rooms
The same, because the total did not change
check.explanation: 1,680 ÷ 20 = 84. Splitting the same total among fewer rooms gives each room more.

connect.modelAnswer: 1,680 ÷ 24 = 70, so each classroom gets 70 pencils. Check by multiplying back: 24 × 70 = 1,680.

exitTicket.explanation: 16 × 147 = 2,352. Running the cycle: 23 ÷ 16 → 1 with 7 left, 75 ÷ 16 → 4 with 11 left, 112 ÷ 16 → 7 with 0 left, so the quotient is 147 with no remainder.
exitTicket.hint: Think through the problem step by step.
choiceFeedback: Re-multiply your answer by 16; does it return to 2,352?
Close — check the remainder and the ones place of your quotient.
hints: Size it up first: 16 × 100 = 1,600 and 16 × 200 = 3,200, so the quotient lands somewhere between 100 and 200.
Set it up as 16 ⟌ 2,352 and run the cycle: divide, multiply, subtract, bring down.
DIVIDE: 23 ÷ 16 → 1. MULTIPLY: 1 × 16 = 16. SUBTRACT: 23 − 16 = 7. BRING DOWN the 5 to make 75, then repeat until the last digit is used.

parallelPractice.stem: Divide 324 by 6. Give the quotient and remainder.
hints: Re-read the question. What exactly is it asking you to find?
Use the visual model, then complete one step at a time.
Start like this: 6 fits into 324 about 54 times.
parallelPractice.explanation: 6 fits into 324 about 54 times. Multiply back: 6 × 54 = 324. The amount left is 0.

hintsEs: Vuelve a leer la pregunta. ¿Qué te pide encontrar exactamente?
Usa el modelo visual y completa un paso a la vez.
Empieza así: 6 cabe en 324 aproximadamente 54 veces.
parallelPractice.explanationEs: 6 cabe en 324 aproximadamente 54 veces. Multiplica para comprobar: 6 × 54 = 324. La cantidad que sobra es 0.

questions.stem: What is the LCM of 4 and 10?
questions.explanation: Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, ... Multiples of 10: 10, 20, ... The smallest common multiple is 20.

questions.stem: What is the LCM of 3 and 5?
